subject: Combined FERPA + GLBA addenda for school-run loan program — feasibility and next steps
related_account: Maple Ridge Unified School District / GroveBank (financial partner)
messages:
From: Elaine Smith <elaine.smith@mapleridge.edu>
To: ben_carter@redwoodai.com
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Question: can Redwood support FERPA + GLBA for our student loan program?

Hi Ben,

Quick intro — I'm Elaine, Director of Student Financial Services at Maple Ridge USD. We're piloting a managed student loan product with GroveBank as the servicing bank. The pilot collects student identifiers and limited financial account info to process payments — so our legal team is telling us we need FERPA protections for education records and GLBA protections for the banking side.

High-level asks: can Redwood sign a combined FERPA + GLBA addendum or implement controls that satisfy both (e.g., residency guarantees, subprocessor restrictions, audit evidence)? We have timeline pressure — vendor selection needs to be finalized by end of July.

Specific items they flagged:
- Subprocessor disclosure + residency for EU/US data (we're US but some parents live abroad)
- BAA/FERPA carve-outs around deidentified datasets used for model improvements
- SOC 2 and pen-test reports for procurement packet
- A pathway where the bank (GroveBank) can access logs for transaction troubleshooting without exposing student PHI/education records

Can you advise feasibility and whether Dedicated or Private deployment would be required? Happy to schedule a quick call.

Thanks,
Elaine
Director, Student Financial Services
Maple Ridge Unified School District
[Attachment: RFP-scoping-sheet.pdf]

From: laura_bennett@redwoodai.com
To: ben_carter@redwoodai.com, Elaine Smith <elaine.smith@mapleridge.edu>
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwoodai.com
Date: Fri, 19 Jun 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Question: can Redwood support FERPA + GLBA for our student loan program? — legal view

Thanks for the ping, Ben. Elaine, hi — quick legal read:

- Contractual stance: We can produce a combined addendum that addresses FERPA and GLBA obligations. Key items we'll need to negotiate: data classification (what counts as "education record" vs bank "financial record"), permitted use / model training carve-outs, and audit/third-party access definitions.

- Residency & subprocessors: We can offer US-only residency for tenant data and restrict cross-border transfers unless explicitly authorized. For GroveBank, we can provide a limited, redacted log feed for transaction troubleshooting under an NDA and narrow purpose clause.

- Deployment: Private (VPC) or Dedicated are the typical paths for customers requiring contractual residency and restricted subprocessor surfaces. Hosted could work only with strict DPA language and customers willing to accept our standard subprocessor list — not ideal for this use-case.

- Evidence: We'll provide SOC 2 Type II and our pen-test summary for procurement; full reports may require an NDA.

I attached a redlined DPA skeleton with placeholders for the FERPA/GLBA clauses and a proposed federated architecture diagram that describes how we can isolate the bank-facing pipeline from education records.

Happy to join the call next week to walk through practical tradeoffs.

— Laura
Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_dpa_v3_redline.pdf]
[Attachment: proposed_federated_architecture_diagram.png]

Appreciate the quick responses. A couple of bank-specific clarifications from GroveBank:
- We need to be sure data used for reconciliation/chargebacks can be exported on demand (CSV) with a 30-day RTO.
- Any log-sharing must preserve student identifiers in hashed form unless we have a warrant/legit legal demand channel.
- We will require a copy of Redwood's SOC 2 and a short summary of encryption-at-rest/key management. If Dedicated/VPC is recommended, provide rough pricing delta so procurement can evaluate.

If you can send the SOC 2 and a DocuSign version of the proposed addendum, we can queue our legal review.

— Victor
Director, Vendor Risk Management
GroveBank
